items.text: From singing at concerts to singing 'Happy birthday'.
Around the world, humans have been singing in unison for millennia.
Some anthropologists even think our ancestors may have sung before they could speak.

level1.label: 宾语从句
level1.text: our ancestors may have sung before they could speak

items.text: "Lullabies are sung to children, and then songs are sung at funerals", says Alex Street, from the Cambridge Institute for Music Therapy Research, who thinks that our positive response to music is no accident.

level1.label: 主语
level1.text: Alex Street, from the Cambridge Institute for Music Therapy Research, who thinks that our positive response to music is no accident

level2.label: 定语从句
level2.text: who thinks that our positive response to music is no accident

items.text: Music is not only enjoyable, but beneficial for our health.

level1.label: 表语
level1.text: not only enjoyable, but beneficial for our health

items.text: There is growing evidence that singing can energise us, improve immune function and increase feelings of happiness, according to 'A Review of the Physiological Effects and Mechanisms of Singing', published in 2018.

level1.label: 主语
level1.text: growing evidence that singing can energise us, improve immune function and increase feelings of happiness

level2.label: 同位语从句
level2.text: that singing can energise us, improve immune function and increase feelings of happiness

items.text: It's thought that the repeated and controlled breathing that singing requires releases endorphins, which are chemicals released by the brain associated with pleasure and wellbeing.

level1.label: 主语从句
level1.text: that the repeated and controlled breathing that singing requires releases endorphins

level1.label: 定语从句
level1.text: which are chemicals released by the brain associated with pleasure and wellbeing

items.text: It may even provide a physical workout comparable to a brisk walk.

level1.label: 宾语
level1.text: a physical workout comparable to a brisk walk

items.text: And singing as part of a group or choir may have additional effects.
Researchers in 'The icebreaker effect: singing mediates fast social bonding' found that singing together accelerated faster social cohesion among strangers.

level1.label: 主语
level1.text: Researchers in 'The icebreaker effect: singing mediates fast social bonding'

level1.label: 宾语从句
level1.text: that singing together accelerated faster social cohesion among strangers

items.text: Some studies have also found that regular musical activity can help to delay the onset of various neurological conditions such as Parkinson's disease and dementia.

level1.label: 宾语从句
level1.text: that regular musical activity can help to delay the onset of various neurological conditions such as Parkinson's disease and dementia

items.text: And it's not too late for those already living with such conditions.
Cathy McGlynn is a music therapist based in Ireland who leads a choir of people with Parkinson's.

level1.label: 表语
level1.text: a music therapist based in Ireland who leads a choir of people with Parkinson's

level2.label: 定语从句
level2.text: who leads a choir of people with Parkinson's

items.text: The disease can lead to respiratory and vocal problems, both of which are benefited by singing practice.

For those suffering with dementia, singing can enhance the type of memory which helps us recall names and specific personal experiences, according to a literature review on singing and cognitive health called 'A Song for the Mind'.

level1.label: 宾语
level1.text: the type of memory which helps us recall names and specific personal experiences

level2.label: 定语从句
level2.text: which helps us recall names and specific personal experiences

items.text: Music therapist Grace Meadows watched as a woman with dementia got up out of her chair and started dancing at a musical performance.

level1.label: 宾语从句
level1.text: as a woman with dementia got up out of her chair and started dancing at a musical performance

items.text: "It was the first time the carers had ever seen her move, unaided."

level1.label: 表语
level1.text: the first time the carers had ever seen her move, unaided

level2.label: 定语从句
level2.text: the carers had ever seen her move, unaided

items.text: Music may not be a medicine in the traditional sense, but one thing seems clear: humans are wired for connection, and music helps to create it.

level1.label: 表语
level1.text: a medicine in the traditional sense

items.text: So, if you're sceptical about the power of music, it may be time to change your tune.

level1.label: 条件状语从句
level1.text: if you're sceptical about the power of music
